items.title: Phase estimation on a superposition of eigenspaces
items.statement_or_definition: For a unit input ψ=Σ_θΠ_θψ, put a_y(θ)=Q^{-1}Σ_(j=0)^(Q−1)exp(2πij(θ−y/Q)) and K_y=Σ_θ a_y(θ)Π_θ. The finite QPE instrument on the system has outcome y with unnormalized state K_y|ψ⟩ and probability p_y=Σ_θ|a_y(θ)|²||Π_θψ||². If p_y>0 its conditional vector is K_yψ/√p_y; if p_y=0 that branch has no conditional state. For a density operator ρ including a reference R, the instrument is (K_y⊗I_R)ρ(K_y†⊗I_R)/p_y. The outcome law is an eigenspace-weighted mixture, but finite-precision conditioning generally retains coherent components of several eigenspaces. Only exact-grid phases with disjoint readout labels yield the corresponding spectral projection.
proof_obligations: Derive the amplitude multiplier a_y by the controlled-power and inverse-QFT matrix, retaining complex phases. Orthogonal Π_θ give K_y†K_y=Σ_θ|a_y(θ)|²Π_θ and Σ_y K_y†K_y=I from the normalized finite geometric kernel. This proves positivity, normalization, reference extension and the conditional state formula. Cross terms vanish in the outcome trace, not in the conditional operator.
